% RFV0-003: give the last full solution sufficient space before chapter break. Layout only.
\enlargethispage{3\baselineskip}
\noindent\textbf{Solution to Exercise~\ref{ex:breadth-karoubi-monic-inclusion}.}
Assume $u$ is monic in $\mathcal C$.  For any object
$(X,e)$ of the completion, let
$h,k:(X,e)\to J(A)$ satisfy $J(u)\circ h=J(u)\circ k$.
The equality is an equality $u h=u k$ of arrows
$X\to B$ in $\mathcal C$.  Since $u$ is monic,
$h=k$ there, and hence in the completion.

This proves
$J(u)$ monic using every new test object $(X,e)$.

% ReadFlow R1 localized pagination: keep the final exercise solution with its preceding page.
\enlargethispage{3\baselineskip}
\paragraph{Solution.}
The numerator magnitude is two, giving
$-2\leq_F-2/5\leq_F2$ and strict bounds
$-3<_F-2/5<_F3$.
For a family the canonical numerator is the existing
projection $a:F\to Z$, so $|a|$ and $s|a|$ are
composites of supplied arrows. The proved inequalities
hold on $F$ itself and restrict by any map into it.
No independent choice of a numerical bound at each
point is made.
